headline: Weakest fiscal quarter posts a loss on rising fleet costs
summary_short: U-Haul's fiscal Q4 2026 revenue (period ended March 31, 2026) fell 10.2% q/q to $1,271.8M but rose 3.1% y/y, while the company swung to a $127.8M net loss (-$0.70 diluted EPS) from a $37.0M profit last quarter, hit by rising depreciation, fleet-disposal losses, and interest expense.
summary_long: Revenue was $1,271.8M, down 10.2% q/q but up 3.1% y/y — consistent with U-Haul's stated seasonality (Q4 is its weakest quarter). EBITDA rose 54.2% y/y to $340.5M yet operating income swung to -$154.9M as full-year (FY2026) depreciation rose $186.6M and fleet-disposal losses rose $117.6M on lower resale values; interest expense grew to $364.8M from $295.7M. Net income swung to a $127.8M loss (-$0.70 diluted EPS) from a $37.0M profit q/q. Cash rose to $1,120.1M (+8.5% q/q, +13.3% y/y). Fiscal 2027 outlook is qualitative only — no numeric guidance — with fleet and storage-development spending both expected to decrease.

drivers.explanation: 10-K covers fiscal 2026 (not this quarter alone): consolidated earnings from operations fell $283.5M to $432.6M as depreciation, fleet-disposal losses, and operating costs outpaced revenue growth, per the MD&A's FY2026-vs-FY2025 comparison.

FY2026 self-moving equipment revenue rose $86.4M on higher one-way transactions and In-Town revenue per transaction; self-storage revenue rose $74.5M on occupancy gains and 5% higher revenue per occupied foot (full fiscal-year figures).

FY2026 rental-fleet depreciation rose $186.6M and net losses on truck disposals rose $117.6M as resale values fell; personnel costs (+$61.3M) and self-insured liability costs (+$76.4M) also rose, per the annual MD&A.
Interest expense rose to $364.8M from $295.7M on higher average debt and cost of debt; income tax expense fell to $29.5M from $110.4M. Both are full fiscal-year figures per the release.

FY2026 operating cash flow rose $340.2M (incl. $119.4M of tax refunds) and investing outflow fell $628.0M as PP&E purchases fell and fleet-sale proceeds rose, lifting full-year cash $131.3M to $1,120.1M.
